modules.name: Deliverables, hard-rules, gates and deadline tracker
modules.design_question: Which VTC hard rules, process gates (eligibility included) and recommended deliverables are met, missing or at risk, and how long remains to the closing instant 2026-11-30T23:59Z (16:59 Vancouver)?
inputs: brief_register: team copy of the English brief PDF (language version, filename, SHA-256; the site plans and 3D model listed under the brief download are hashed too) plus transcribed rules {id, value, exact|max, page, transcribed_by, checked_by} and site_placement {lon, lat, grid_rotation_deg, source brief_site_plan|brief_3d_model|team_placement, page}; seeded from the project description (amber until page and second check are entered)

document_register (DATA-packet interface): brief (every language version the team downloaded; English treated as governing until C9 is answered), Terms HTML snapshot hash, jury-panel snapshot from the competition page (names, practices; hash and date), 1997 Higher Buildings Policy, Public Views Guidelines, Open Government Licence - Vancouver text, each with SHA-256 and retrieval date

rule_registry: one record per rule id {id, class, clause, value, evidence_status verified|unverified|team_assumption, history[] of flag ids, correction log}; complete id list: hard rules HR-01, HR-02, HR-02t, HR-03, HR-03a, HR-04, HR-05, HR-06; gates G-00..G-04; release control G-05; deadline D-01..D-03; register B-01..B-03; coverage R-01. P13-M01, P13-M03 and P13-M06 read it; a schema test fails the build if any metric cites an id that is not in the registry

eligibility_register (G-00): per member attestation of Terms 3.3.1-3.3.5 (age, sanctions, no employment, internship, contract, officer or director role with the Organizer or any listed juror or their practice, no family or associate relation) and the organiser's written answer to C8 {date, text, answered_by}; stays private to the team
portal_observations {ask_the_jury available|absent|unknown, observed_on, Q&A deadline shown on the portal}; null = unknown, so the organiser contact is used
board_layout from P13-M06a (frames, element tags, text frames) OR a manual placement list {item, board} typed by the team (optional port; null = manual list)
export_manifest from P13-M06v validator or P13-M06b composer (bytes, px, ratio, sha256, subsampling, scan mode, checks[], anonymity_findings[], juror_warnings[])

editable checklist: 6 hard rules (JPEG, size, panel count, A2 landscape ratio, English, anonymity), 5 gates (G-00 eligibility; G-01 UIC validated and identity verified; G-02 N sign-offs; G-03 rights register and licence pack complete; G-04 no public or juror-seen board-linked asset), the G-05 upload-once release control, and 20 recommended items (3 diagrams: programme, structure, massing; 3 studies: wind, solar/shadow, sustainability; site plan; ground floor plan; 3 typical plans; 2 sections; skyline view; mid-city view; 4 ground-level perspectives; policy reflection)
module result cards from other packets (wind, shadow, sustainability, structure, programme)
rubric gaps from P13-M07 (optional port, advisory; null = no gaps)
rights_status, asset_visibility and review_audience_log from P13-M08a
signoff_count N (default 2 for teams, 1 for individuals)
qa_register: questions sent, channel, answers with dates (non-binding)
current UTC time, deadline instant 2026-11-30T23:59:00Z, team time zone
outputs: submission_status (typed JSON: hard_rules[], gates[] incl. G-00, coverage, missing[], days_left, blocking, brief_sha256, brief_language, rule_registry_version)
blocking_issues list consumed by the release gate P13-M06c
dated rule changelog (organiser answers logged as dated clarifications; Ask the Jury answers, if the service is offered, logged as non-binding; brief, Terms and jury-panel re-reads with hashes)
task_timeline: dated human tasks with owner and status (C8 and C9, eligibility attestations, identity verification, brief register, Q&A pack, registration, re-reads, single upload)
qa_pack: one row per open flag {question, clause quoted, channel organiser_contact (default) | ask_the_jury (only if portal_observations says available), owner, due, answer, answered_on}

parameters.name: panel_count_rule
parameters.relationship: Terms 4.8 defer the count to the brief (one to four). Exact 4 fails a 3-board entry; a maximum reading passes it. Default exact 4, as transcribed from the brief, until the register is double-checked.

parameters.name: recommended_item_set
parameters.relationship: Each unplaced recommended item lowers coverage. Team mapping to jury criteria: missing ground-level views weakens human-scale evidence (40%); missing wind, solar or sustainability studies weakens design-excellence evidence (20%).

parameters.name: deadline_instant
parameters.relationship: Page: 23:59 London (GMT in November) = 2026-11-30T23:59Z = 16:59 Vancouver (UTC-7). Terms 4.7 says 24.00 London. The earlier instant is used because late entries are automatically disqualified (8.4).

parameters.name: registration_close
parameters.relationship: Closes 29 Oct 2026 (hour not stated). Identity verification precedes payment and UIC (3.6.A.1-A.2), verification fees are non-refundable once started (7.4.1) and fees are not reclaimable (7.3), so G-00 comes first. Static banner.

parameters.name: upload_lock
parameters.relationship: After the first upload, edits need a paid reactivation fee (Terms 4.7, 7.7) and the entry may go to early evaluation. Export early, but upload once, when every gate passes.

parameters.name: file_size_margin
parameters.relationship: A bigger margin below 10 MB protects against MB/MiB ambiguity and portal overhead but forces lower JPEG quality or fewer pixels, which softens thin linework.

parameters.name: aspect_ratio_tolerance
parameters.relationship: A2 is 420 x 594 mm (ratio 1.414). A tighter tolerance prevents stretched or cropped boards; a looser one hides layout mistakes.

parameters.name: language_allow_list
parameters.relationship: The page requires English; a literal check would reject Nation names. Explanatory text must be English; reviewed names pass with an English gloss. Spellings vary between sources, so each entry is reviewed and Unicode-normalised.

parameters.name: signoff_count
parameters.relationship: Terms 3.2 define teams of two to four, but individual entry exists (2.4, 3.6.A.4). With N=2 no author can release alone; an individual sets N=1 and may add a second reader who sees no identifying data.

parameters.name: terms_reread_interval
parameters.relationship: The organiser may alter the Terms and the brief at any time (9.1; 16.2 covers the Terms). A shorter interval catches changes sooner but costs reviewer time; each re-read stores a hash and logs differences.

parameters.name: qa_question_budget
parameters.relationship: Ask the Jury exists only for selected competitions (10.10.1) and the VTC page lists none, so questions default to the organiser contact. If the portal shows it: one free question per registration (10.10.3.1), more paid (10.10.3.2), answers non-binding.

parameters.name: eligibility_attestation
parameters.relationship: Terms 3.3.5 bars staff of the Organizer or Jury and their associates or family; 'associate' is undefined and a listed juror is at UBC SALA. False eligibility data disqualifies (8.1). G-00 stays red until all members attest and the organiser's answer is logged.

metrics.name: Panel file format
metrics.good: every panel is .jpg/.jpeg
metrics.bad: any PDF, PNG, TIFF or other format
metrics.method: Check extension and JPEG magic bytes (FF D8 FF) of each exported board.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-01 | evidence: verified | history: none] Terms 4.8 (re-read r3): each panel must be saved as JPEG (.jpg or .jpeg); non-compliance may lead to disqualification (8.2).

metrics.name: Panel file size (hard limit)
metrics.good: <= 10^7 bytes (stricter reading of 10 MB)
metrics.method: Read byte length of each exported JPEG.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-02 | evidence: verified | history: none] Terms 4.8: size must not exceed 10 megabytes (MB); MB is not defined, so the tool applies the stricter 10^7 bytes.

metrics.name: Panel file size (team target)
metrics.good: <= 9.5 x 10^6 bytes
metrics.bad: amber between 9.5 x 10^6 and 10^7 bytes; red above 10^7
metrics.method: Same byte count compared with a margin that is safe under either MB definition.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-02t | evidence: team assumption] Team margin; editable.

metrics.name: Panel count upper bound
metrics.good: 1 to 4 panels
metrics.method: Count exported boards.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-03a | evidence: verified | history: none] Terms 4.8: the brief sets a single panel or up to four panels.

metrics.name: Panel count required by the brief
metrics.good: equals the brief_register value (default exact 4)
metrics.bad: differs from the register, or register empty (amber until the PDF is hashed)
metrics.method: Compare board count with the brief_register panel rule (exact or max).
metrics.basis: [rule HR-03 | evidence now: unverified until the register holds hash, page and second check | history: r1 'verified' from team text; r2 the team holds the PDF, so this is a due task (23-24 Oct), not a tool limit; r3 the register also records the language version (F41)] Project description states four boards from the brief.

metrics.name: Board aspect ratio / orientation
metrics.good: landscape, width:height = 1.414 +/- 0.005 (594 x 420 mm)
metrics.method: width_px / height_px of each JPEG.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-04 | evidence now: A2 = 420 x 594 mm verified (ISO 216); landscape unverified until register; tolerance is a team choice | history: r1 corrected; r2 same record shown in P13-M06] The same rule id is used in both modules.

metrics.name: Language
metrics.good: all explanatory text English; every non-English token on the reviewed allow-list with an English gloss
metrics.bad: non-English explanatory text, or an unreviewed non-English token
metrics.method: Attestation per text frame in P13-M06a (language='en', two members) plus allow-list, OCR-language and glyph checks from P13-M06v/b.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-05 | evidence: page requirement verified; allow-list reading is a team assumption] The competition page requires English; admitting Nation names via an allow-list is the team's reading, to confirm with the organiser (Q1).

metrics.name: Anonymity of the exported boards
metrics.good: 0 class-A findings in file name, metadata and OCR text (class W juror-name warnings cleared with a logged reason), and a logged human visual check per board
metrics.bad: >= 1 class-A finding or a board without the visual check; an uncleared class-W warning is amber
metrics.method: Read anonymity_findings[] and juror_warnings[] from the manifest and the per-board visual-check flag from P13-M06c.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-06 | evidence: verified rule | tool method is team design] Terms 5.1 bars marks, logos, symbols or signs that may identify the source; 5.3 says the jury learns identities only after winners are selected; 5.2 and 8.3 bar approaching or communicating with jurors.

metrics.name: Eligibility and no-contact attestation (Terms 3.3, 5.2, 8.3)
metrics.good: every member attests to 3.3.1-3.3.5 and no jury contact, and the organiser's written answer on school affiliation (C8) is logged
metrics.bad: any member unattested or C8 unanswered (red); every member logging 'risk accepted' on an unanswered C8 shows amber, never green
metrics.method: Manual attestation per member stored in eligibility_register; C8 answer logged with date and sender; the gate stays red until both are present.
metrics.basis: [rule G-00 | evidence: clause text verified (Terms 3.3, 5.2, 8.3 read r3); applicability to students of a juror's school unverified | history: r1-r2 assumed no eligibility check beyond identity and team size (F38)] Terms 3.3: a participant or team member who is or becomes an employee, intern, contractor, officer or director of the Organizer or the Jury, or an associate or family member thereof (3.3.5), is disqualified and forfeits all prizes; 'associate' is undefined; 7.3 and 7.4.1: fees not refundable. The competition page lists a juror as 'Matthew Soules Architecture, UBC SALA'; sala.ubc.ca lists him as a Professor.

metrics.name: Upload prerequisites (UIC, identity)
metrics.good: UIC validated and every member verified at the moment of UIC validation or team joining
metrics.bad: any member unverified or no UIC
metrics.method: Manual attestation of portal status by two members; stricter reading also asks for active status at release.
metrics.basis: [rule G-01 | evidence: verified] Terms 3.6.A.1 and 3.6.C.1: verification on Architects' Network before UIC validation or team joining; 3.6.A.2: fee paid after verification; 3.6.C.1: active status is required only at that moment. The how-to-enter page says verification is required before upload.

metrics.name: Sign-off count (release)
metrics.good: N distinct members signed (N = signoff_count)
metrics.method: Count signed entries in the release log.
metrics.basis: [rule G-02 | evidence: tool design] Terms 3.2 (teams of two to four) and 2.4/3.6.A.4 (individual entry) set who can enter; the sign-off count is a team control.

metrics.name: Rights register and licence pack complete
metrics.good: every placed raster has a known licence compatible with Terms 12.2 and 12.7
metrics.method: Read rights_status from P13-M08a.
metrics.basis: [rule G-03 | evidence: verified] Terms 4.3 lets the organiser demand licences, failure may disqualify; 12.2 and 12.7 grant perpetual licences.

metrics.name: No public or juror-seen board-linked asset before closing
metrics.good: 0 board-linked assets with visibility public before 2026-11-30T23:59Z, and the review_audience_log shows no listed juror among the viewers of any board-linked asset
metrics.bad: >= 1 public asset linked to a board element, or a listed juror among the viewers of one
metrics.method: Join placements with P13-M08a asset_visibility and review_audience_log; the juror_register comes from the jury-panel snapshot in the document_register.
metrics.basis: [rule G-04 | evidence: tool design; clauses verified | history: r3 adds juror exposure] Terms 4.1: visual materials must not have been previously published by any member; 5.2, 5.3, 8.3: no approaching or communicating with the Jury, identities hidden until winners; Buildner asks resubmissions to be newly prepared and visually distinct. Whether a course review with a juror present counts is unresolved (C8).

metrics.name: Registration close warning
metrics.good: > 8 days to 29 Oct, or UIC already validated
metrics.bad: <= 8 days with no UIC: amber; <= 2 days: red; G-00 still unresolved at <= 3 days: red
metrics.method: 29 Oct 2026 minus now, shown only while no UIC is recorded; delivered as a static banner on 21 Oct, not as a 6 Nov widget.
metrics.basis: [rule D-02 | evidence: team thresholds] 8 days is the time left on 21 Oct 2026; the closing hour is not stated on the page.

metrics.name: Upload-once gate
metrics.good: first upload only after all hard rules and gates (G-00..G-04) pass and N members sign
metrics.method: P13-M06c unlocks the package only when blocking=false, N sign-offs and visual checks are logged.
metrics.basis: [rule G-05 | evidence: verified] Terms 4.7: after the first upload the participant may not modify, replace, edit or re-upload without the paid reactivation; the gate itself is tool design.

metrics.name: Recommended-item coverage
metrics.good: 20 of 20 items placed (counts met: 3 typical plans, >= 2 sections, >= 4 ground-level views)
metrics.bad: any category with zero items placed
metrics.method: Match checklist items to tagged board elements in board_layout, or to the manual placement list when M06a is absent.
metrics.basis: [rule R-01 | evidence: item list from the project description, unverified until the register] Items are 'recommended', so a gap is not a rule breach and the cut-off is a team choice.

metrics.name: Days of buffer before closing
metrics.good: >= 7 days between 'all hard rules pass' and the closing instant
metrics.bad: <= 2 days, or any hard-rule failure within 7 days
metrics.method: deadline_instant minus now, shown in London (GMT) and Vancouver (UTC-7).
metrics.basis: [rule D-01 | evidence: instant verified | history: r1 text converted the close to 15:59 PST; BC is on UTC-7, so 16:59] The 7-day and 2-day buffers are team choices; late entries are automatically disqualified (8.4).

metrics.name: Time-zone data check
metrics.good: offset parsed from Intl formatToParts (longOffset 'GMT-07:00' -> -420 min; 'GMT' = 0) equals -420 for America/Vancouver at 2026-11-30T23:59Z
metrics.bad: any other value: browser tzdata predates 2026b, use fixed -07:00 and warn
metrics.method: Format the instant with timeZoneName 'longOffset', read the timeZoneName part, strip 'GMT', convert to minutes and compare with -420.
metrics.basis: [rule D-03 | evidence: verified | history: r1 compared the string with '-07:00', which never matches because longOffset returns 'GMT-07:00'] tzdb 2026b put BC on permanent -07; latest release 2026e (2026-09-29) makes no further BC change.

metrics.name: Brief register integrity
metrics.good: English PDF stored with SHA-256 and filename, every rule has a page reference and a second-person check, site_placement recorded, Terms and jury-panel hashes re-read within terms_reread_interval
metrics.bad: any rule without page reference or second check, no language version recorded, or a Terms or jury-panel hash that changed unread
metrics.method: Validate the register JSON; compare Terms, brief and jury-panel hashes at each re-read; other language versions are hashed and compared only when a figure seems to conflict.
metrics.basis: [rule B-01 | evidence: team control] The organiser may alter the Terms and the brief (9.1; 16.2 covers the Terms only, re-read r3); the page offers the brief in five languages and neither page nor Terms says which governs (C9).

metrics.name: Q&A pack coverage
metrics.good: every open flag has a question, channel (organiser contact by default), owner and due date: C8 and C9 sent by Fri 23 Oct, all others by Fri 30 Oct
metrics.bad: any open flag without them, or Ask the Jury used as the only channel
metrics.method: Join qa_register with the UNRESOLVED flags; read portal_observations for channel availability (null = organiser contact).
metrics.basis: [rule B-02 | evidence: team control; channel facts verified | history: r2 routed Q1 to 'Ask the Jury' (F35)] Terms 10.10.1: Ask the Jury only for selected competitions; the page sends all communication to Buildner staff and closes Q&A on 3 Nov. Terms 10.10.4.1 default is three days after registration closes (1 Nov) unless otherwise specified on the Competition Portal; whether the page counts as the portal is unresolved, so the team cut-off is the earlier date.

visualization: Checklist grid: 20 recommended-item rows x up to 4 board columns with green/amber/red chips; hard rules and gates (G-00 to G-04) as pass/fail badges linked to their clause (e.g., Terms 3.3.5, 4.8) and to the rule id; G-00 shows amber 'risk accepted' separately from green

Dual-time countdown (London GMT / Vancouver UTC-7) on a timeline with ticks for 23 Oct (C8, C9 sent), 29 Oct registration close, 30 Oct question deadline (team), 3 Nov Q&A close, 6/13 Nov deliveries, 30 Nov 16:59 Vancouver / 23:59 London; superseded text (15:59) shown struck through
Four board thumbnails with ghost slots for missing items, a byte gauge (bytes against 10^7 and the 9.5 x 10^6 target) and an upload-once panel listing open gates
Dated human-task list (eligibility attestation, C8/C9, identity verification, register, Q&A, re-reads) with owner and done/overdue chips
modules.method: Load a versioned JSON: brief_register (language version, site_placement), rule_registry (hard rules, gates G-00..G-04, deadline; each with evidence_status and history[]), 20 items with jury tag and minimum count, eligibility_register, qa_register and task_timeline. Typed nodes read evidence_status, never the display status. Hard rules read export_manifest from the validator or composer; language is attestation per text frame plus allow-list, OCR and glyph checks. Coverage = items whose minimum count is met in board tags or the manual placement list / 20. The deadline is a UTC instant; the Vancouver offset is parsed from formatToParts (strip 'GMT', empty = 0) and compared in minutes with -420, else a fixed offset and a warning. Any rule or gate failure, including unresolved G-00, sets blocking=true, which P13-M06c obeys. Optional ports have defined null behaviour. Thresholds show their source or an amber 'team assumption' tag; edits are logged; answers and re-read hashes become dated changelog entries.
modules.human_judgment: Reading the full brief and Terms and transcribing the rules twice; each member's honest eligibility attestation and whether to pay fees while C8 is open; whether an item truly answers the brief (a wind study must be an analysis, not a label); which recommended items to omit and justify; writing and sending the questions; the single upload through the Buildner portal and the final sign-off.
modules.limits: The spec authors did not open the brief PDF; the team holds it, and the rules shown are the project description's transcription until the register is double-checked. The portal may apply undocumented checks (pixels, colour mode, MB vs MiB, progressive JPEG); a live test upload is unsafe (4.7). The tool records attestations and organiser answers but cannot judge eligibility or the undefined 'associate'. Coverage counts presence, not quality.

libraries.name: Intl.DateTimeFormat (browser built-in)
libraries.role: London/Vancouver conversion; longOffset parsed through formatToParts, offset self-check

libraries.name: Web Crypto API (SubtleCrypto.digest, browser built-in)
libraries.role: SHA-256 of brief, Terms snapshot, jury-panel snapshot and exported JPEGs

modules.effort: S-M: core 5.5 person-days: 4 by 6 Nov (rule registry with evidence_status and schema test, brief_register, hard rules from the validator, G-00 eligibility, gates, deadline, manual placement list), 1.5 by 13 Nov (language and anonymity glue, qa_register, task timeline). Human tasks (about 2.5 person-days) are budgeted separately in Tier A. The registration banner is static text.

modules.name: Drawing extraction (plans, sections, make2d-style linework)
modules.design_question: Can plans, sections and the site plan be produced from the model as scaled, layered linework that fits the board frame, including a full-height tower section, and reconciles with programme areas?
inputs: Layer 0 meshes / B-reps with program tags (from imports: Rhino 3dm, OBJ, IFC, SketchUp, Revit)
storey elevations, floor-to-floor heights and below-grade depth (programme / structure modules)
cut plane and section line definitions chosen by user
site north rotation angle (SITE packet)
frame size in mm and target scale from P13-M06a (board_layout)
optional: Rhino Make2D SVG/DXF exported by the user from desktop Rhino (v0 route)
outputs: drawing_set[]: {id, type plan|section|elevation|site_plan, svg, scale, cut_height, bbox_mm, fit_pct, layers by program tag, line classes} consumed by P13-M06b
gfa_by_storey reconciliation result for programme modules
DXF/SVG export for use in Rhino/Illustrator

parameters.name: cut_height_above_floor
parameters.relationship: Plans are conventionally cut about 1.2 m (4 ft) above finished floor, showing walls, openings and columns; a cut at slab level hides openings, one above head height loses wall and door relationships.

parameters.name: section_line_position
parameters.relationship: A section through the core and public volumes shows how public-facing uses stack vertically through the tower, which the brief asks for; a section through blank floors hides it.

parameters.name: plan_scale
parameters.relationship: Printed extent = real size / n. The 144.8 m block side is 290 mm at 1:500 but 724 mm at 1:200, beyond the 420 mm board height; a smaller scale frees area but shrinks annotation legibility.

parameters.name: section_scale
parameters.relationship: Printed height = H/n. A 305 m tower plus about 20 m below grade (illustration) is 650 mm at 1:500, over the 420 mm board height, and 325 mm at 1:1000; podium sections at 1:200-1:500 need partial cuts.

parameters.name: site_plan_extent
parameters.relationship: A site plan with the block, arterial, high street, lanes and the transit plaza across is about 250-350 m (team estimate, to measure on the brief's site plan): 500-700 mm at 1:500 (over the board), 250-350 mm at 1:1000.

parameters.name: hidden_lines_on
parameters.relationship: Make2D writes hidden lines to separate layers that can be dashed or hidden. The browser route returns visible edges only; hidden edges there need a new, untested pass, so the class stays Make2D-only until a pilot comparison passes.

parameters.name: input_route
parameters.relationship: Make2D runs in desktop Rhino; a server needs Rhino.Compute on Windows Server with core-hour billing (US$0.10 per core-hour), so v0 imports its SVG/DXF. The mesh route projects along one axis per view; IFC can use IfcOpenShell on a server.

parameters.name: reconciliation_level
parameters.relationship: Summing areas at the 1.2 m cut measures wall lines and openings; slab-edge loops at floor level track floor area. The zoning floor-area definition is unsourced, so tolerances are team values.

parameters.name: crease_angle_threshold
parameters.relationship: UNRESOLVED: relationship between edge-angle threshold and drawing clarity on curved facades was not found in an opened source (see unresolved_relationships).

metrics.name: Plan cut height convention
metrics.good: 1.2 m (about 4 ft) above finished floor
metrics.bad: cut at slab level (0 m) or above 1.8 m
metrics.method: Compare chosen cut with the convention.
metrics.basis: Good value is the stated convention; the bad bounds are the team's reading of 'approximately'.

metrics.name: Cut-loop closure ratio
metrics.good: 100% of cut polylines closed (poche can fill)
metrics.method: closed cut loops / all cut loops after slicing Layer 0 with the cut plane.
metrics.basis: Open loops indicate non-watertight Layer 0 geometry; thresholds are team-set.

metrics.name: Drawing fits allocated frame
metrics.good: scaled bbox <= 100% of frame in both axes (sections use tower height plus below-grade depth)
metrics.method: bbox_mm = model extent / scale, compared with the frame in mm on a 594 x 420 mm board; shown at preset selection, not only after export.
metrics.basis: Arithmetic: 144.8 m at 1:500 = 290 mm; a 325 m section is 650 mm at 1:500 and 325 mm at 1:1000.

metrics.name: Site plan extent fit
metrics.good: site-plan window fits its frame (default 1:1000: 250-350 mm for 250-350 m) with a 1:500 inset of the block (290 mm for the 144.8 m side)
metrics.bad: > 100% of frame in either axis, e.g. a 700 m window at 1:500 does not fit
metrics.method: window_m / scale compared with the frame in mm; the window size is entered by the team from the brief's site plan.
metrics.basis: Arithmetic is exact; the 250-350 m window is a team estimate until measured.

metrics.name: Segments per drawing
metrics.good: <= 250,000 line segments
metrics.method: Count after linework simplification.
metrics.basis: No published budget; chosen so rasterising a board stays fast. Tune after testing.

metrics.name: Area reconciliation with programme tags
metrics.good: |slab-edge area - tagged GFA| <= 1% per storey
metrics.method: Sum polygon areas of slab-edge loops at floor level per storey versus Layer 0 tag totals; state the GFA definition used.
metrics.basis: Team tolerance; the Vancouver floor-area definition (zoning exclusions) was not opened, so it stays a team assumption until PROG sources it.

metrics.name: Line-weight hierarchy
metrics.good: cut > silhouette > projected edge > hidden with each step about 2:1
metrics.bad: two classes drawn at the same weight
metrics.method: Class-to-weight table rendered in the SVG stroke-width.
metrics.basis: Common drafting convention recalled from ISO 128-20, which was not opened; weights are editable presets.

metrics.name: Line classes available by route
metrics.good: Make2D import: cut, silhouette, tangent and hidden layers; browser edge projection: cut, silhouette, crease and visible only
metrics.bad: hidden class offered on the browser route without a tested method
metrics.method: List the line classes each route actually returns in the drawing_set.
metrics.basis: [evidence now: verified from READMEs | history: r1 credited Make2D hidden layers to the browser route and cited pdf-lib (S30)] three-edge-projection returns visible lines only.

metrics.name: Hidden-line method validity (browser route)
metrics.good: hidden = edge interval minus collinear visible sub-segments (tolerance), or open edges clipped against closed polygons of nearer faces (Clipper2 open subjects)
metrics.bad: 'difference of open paths from open paths' with Clipper2, which is not supported
metrics.method: Code review plus a unit test on a box-and-slab model with known hidden edges.
metrics.basis: [evidence now: verified from Clipper2 docs | history: r1 proposed clipper2-js difference of segments] Clipper2: only subject paths may be open; clip paths must be closed. P13-S25 uses clipper2-js for silhouette polygons.

metrics.name: Hidden-line agreement with Make2D
metrics.good: length-weighted agreement with a Make2D import of the same model is reported before the hidden class is offered
metrics.bad: hidden class shown with no pilot comparison
metrics.method: Overlay browser hidden class on Make2D hidden layer; report matched length / total within a print-scale tolerance.
metrics.basis: Method untested; thresholds are set after the first pilot, so no number is asserted.

visualization: SVG preview with toggles per line class (cut, silhouette, crease, visible, hidden where available) and per program-tag layer, poche filled with the programme colour
Plan with cut-line markers, rotated site-north arrow and scale bar
Board-frame overlay showing each drawing at 1:n inside its allocated rectangle, with a red overflow warning; the site plan shows its window and the 1:500 inset
Scale ladder: horizontal bars for printed section height at 1:200, 1:500 and 1:1000 and site-plan windows at 1:500, 1:750 and 1:1000 against a vertical line at the 420 mm board height
modules.method: v0 (core): the user exports Rhino Make2D SVG/DXF from desktop Rhino; the tool imports it, maps layers to program tags, fills closed cut loops as poche, scales to 1:n, checks fit (including site_plan_extent) against the M06a frame and writes drawing_set. v1 mesh route: index Layer 0 as meshes; slice plans at the cut height, chain segments, close loops, fill poche; project visible geometry with three-edge-projection (y-axis); sections: rotate so the view axis is y, clip, repeat; classify cut, silhouette, crease, visible; hidden = interval subtraction of visible sub-segments from each projected edge, or clipping against nearer-face polygons (untested, Make2D-only until a pilot passes). Output layered SVG with scale bar and rotated north arrow. Report closure, segments, reconciliation and fit. IFC via IfcOpenShell on a server (roadmap).
modules.human_judgment: Where to cut and section, which elements and levels represent the design, whether to use partial sections, the site-plan window, line weights, annotation and entourage, and whether the drawing tells the story of vertical public uses.
modules.limits: Mesh linework is faceted on curved facades; curtain-wall detail and below-slab structure are absent from Layer 0. three-edge-projection works along one axis, has 12 open issues and returns visible edges only; speed on a 300 m tower is untested. The hidden-line pass is a new, untested method. Make2D needs desktop Rhino or a billed Rhino.Compute server and stays the quality reference.

modules.name: Camera presets and viewpoint library
modules.design_question: From which sourced viewpoints and lenses must the tower be shown (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city, four ground-level views), and which of the City's 24 protected-view cones does it touch?
inputs: site_georeference {lon, lat, grid_rotation_deg, source brief_site_plan|brief_3d_model|team_placement, page} from the P13-M01 brief_register (amber until transcribed with a page number); site footprint, terrain and context models incl. existing and approved towers (SITE packet)
City of Vancouver Open Data 'View cones' dataset: all 24 polygons with view_number and view_cone_name (cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 give the Queen Elizabeth Park viewpoint)
tower heights, massing and tower footprints from Layer 0
site north rotation angle
sun date/time from CLIM packet for lighting
breach_register entries and rationale from P13-M08a (read back for the encroachment report)
outputs: camera_preset[]: {name, position_local, georef_origin, target, hfov, roll, shift, viewpoint_source, eye_height, azimuth} consumed by P13-M04, P13-M05, P13-M06b and CLIM image exports
cone_overlay: apex, bearings and polygon intersection of the site footprint and each tower footprint with every one of the 24 cones

encroachment_report[]: {view_number, view_cone_name, site_overlap_m2, tower_overlap_m2, ceiling_m|null, tower_top_minus_ceiling_m|null, angular_share_of_cone, flips_under_one_block_shift} offered to P13-M08a as breach_register candidates
placement_sensitivity: cones whose intersection changes when the footprint shifts one block in each direction
tower_share_of_frame and context_tower_visibility per preset
compass-labelled overlay data (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet/North Shore Mountains)

parameters.name: viewpoint_position
parameters.relationship: The four QE Park cone polygons share an apex at 49.24216 N, 123.11244 W (re-computed in r2), about 186 m east of Wikipedia's park point. Using the park point shifts the sight line to the tower by up to about 2 degrees at 5 km.

parameters.name: viewpoint_elevation
parameters.relationship: Eye elevation = terrain at the apex (SITE packet) + eye height. Wikipedia's 125 m refers to the park and Little Mountain, not to the apex; a higher eye puts more of the tower above the horizon.

parameters.name: cone_set
parameters.relationship: Cones touched depend on placement: a nominal 1.1 x 0.8 km core window meets 8 of 24, a 2.2 x 1.4 km downtown window 17 (computed r3). Testing only the QE Park cones would miss Cambie 9.1/9.2, Charleson B2, Heather Bay D and Alder Terrace A.

parameters.name: site_georeference
parameters.relationship: Placement decides which cones apply: at a nominal core point, a 145 m shift east or west drops cone 3.2.2 or 3.2.3 (computed r3). Use the brief's site plan or 3D model; otherwise an amber team placement.

parameters.name: cone_fan
parameters.relationship: Development inside a cone is height-limited (dataset text). Cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 are about 10.4, 3.4, 11.8 and 12.6 degrees wide (computed r3); a 145 m face at 4.6 km spans 1.8 degrees, over half of narrow 3.2.2.

parameters.name: viewing_distance
parameters.relationship: Apparent height = atan(height difference / distance). Illustration: a 300 m tower at 5 km subtends about 3.4 degrees, so doubling distance halves its size in frame and forces a longer lens or a crop.

parameters.name: focal_length_equivalent
parameters.relationship: Horizontal field = 2 x atan(18/f): 50 mm gives 39.6 degrees, 85 mm gives 23.9 degrees. Longer lenses enlarge the distant tower in frame but narrow the visible context.

parameters.name: eye_height
parameters.relationship: Ground-level views at about 1.6 m show canopies and podium frontage at pedestrian scale, the scale the human-scale criterion judges; higher cameras read as aerial views.

parameters.name: site_north_rotation
parameters.relationship: The site plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so view azimuths and compass labels must use the rotated north or the labels will point to the wrong landmarks.

parameters.name: local_origin
parameters.relationship: UTM 10N northings near 5.46 million m fall on 0.5 m steps in 32-bit floats (computed), so vertices jitter. Subtract a site-centred origin in double precision before building cameras and meshes.

parameters.name: encroachment_treatment
parameters.relationship: The Higher Buildings Policy sets a process for select developments to encroach on view 3, and the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded. Encroachment into any cone is reported neutrally and needs a rationale entry, not a red score.

metrics.name: Tower share of frame height (QE Park skyline)
metrics.good: >= 10% of image height
metrics.method: Project tower top and base to the image plane; (top_y - base_y)/frame height; auto-suggest focal length to reach the target.
metrics.basis: Team legibility target; no source gives a value.

metrics.name: Viewpoint offset from the City cone apex
metrics.good: <= 10 m from the dataset apex
metrics.bad: > 50 m, or a park centroid used (about 186 m off)
metrics.method: Distance between the preset and the apex derived from the view-cones polygons in the local frame.
metrics.basis: [evidence now: apex derived and re-checked in r2 (records total_count 24; cones 3.2.1, 3.2.3, 3.2.4 share 49.242156 N, 123.112436 W; 3.2.2 differs by about 0.3 m); apex-as-designated-origin is an inference | history: r1 text said the origin was unobtainable] Tolerances are team values.

metrics.name: Protected view cones intersected (all 24)
metrics.good: all 24 cones clipped against the site and tower footprints; each intersecting cone lists view_number, name, overlap m2 and ceiling or 'unknown'
metrics.bad: any of the 24 not computed (r2 computed only 3.2.1-3.2.4)
metrics.method: Clip the site and tower footprints against the 24 polygons in the local frame; any overlap adds an encroachment note to the caption of the affected view.
metrics.basis: [evidence: dataset geometry verified (24 polygons read r3); placement is team-set until the brief is read | history: r2 scoped the check to QE Park cones (F37)] The Review page says protected views 'will not be reviewed or updated', so all 24 stay fixed constraints. Computed r3 for placeholder windows: 8 of 24 meet a 1.1 x 0.8 km core window, 17 of 24 a 2.2 x 1.4 km downtown window.

metrics.name: Site placement declared and sensitivity checked
metrics.good: site_georeference has a source and page (brief site plan or 3D model) and the intersection is re-run with the footprint shifted one block (144.8 m along the long axis, 79.2 m along the short axis) in each direction, with flips reported
metrics.bad: placement undeclared or a team placement without a note, or no sensitivity run
metrics.method: Read site_georeference from brief_register; re-run the cone intersection for the four shifted footprints; list cones whose result changes.
metrics.basis: [rule B-03 | evidence: team control; placement unverified until the brief's site plan or 3D model is read] The page gives only 'within Vancouver's downtown core' and lists site plans and a 3D model under the brief download. Computed r3 at a placeholder core point (49.28375 N, 123.1175 W, not the brief's site): a 145 m shift east or west drops cone 3.2.2 or 3.2.3.

metrics.name: View-cone encroachment report (neutral)
metrics.good: report complete for every intersecting cone: tower top minus ceiling at the site, encroached area and angular share of that cone; every encroachment has a breach-register entry with rationale
metrics.bad: amber only when an encroachment has no rationale or the ceiling is unknown; never red for the encroachment itself
metrics.method: Compare tower top with each cone's ceiling once read from the Public Views Guidelines or confirmed by the City; compute overlap and angular share at that cone's apex; push candidates to P13-M08a.
metrics.basis: [evidence now: ceilings unverified | history: r1 scored a tower above the ceiling as bad (F08); r3 extends the report from 4 to all intersecting cones (F37)] The 1997 policy (search excerpt, not opened) sets a process for select encroachment into view 3; the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded; the dataset has no height fields.

metrics.name: Number of ground-level perspectives
metrics.method: Count presets of type ground.
metrics.basis: [evidence now: unverified until register | history: r1 'verified' from team text] The figure comes from the brief as transcribed in the project description.

metrics.name: Ground-level eye height
metrics.method: Camera z minus local ground z.
metrics.basis: Common adult eye height; team preset, editable.

metrics.name: Vertical convergence
metrics.good: verticals within 0.5 degrees of vertical (shift lens, zero pitch)
metrics.method: Check camera pitch/roll and lens shift.
metrics.basis: Architectural-visualisation convention; team preset.

metrics.name: Context towers present in the context mesh
metrics.good: every existing and approved tower in the frustum is in the mesh and visible or flagged occluded
metrics.method: Compare the SITE packet tower list with ray-cast visibility from each preset.
metrics.basis: The brief (as transcribed) says context includes existing high-rises and future approved towers in the same range.

visualization: Plan map with rotated north arrow, all 24 cone triangles drawn thin grey from their apexes (labelled by view_number), the cones that touch the site filled in a neutral accent with overlap hatched, the four QE Park cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 outlined, the site footprint plus four ghost footprints shifted one block, a wedge for each camera and a dashed line of sight to the tower top
Elevation profile from the viewpoint to the site: terrain line, horizon, tower silhouette, context towers; encroachment shown as a neutral grey band with its height value, never red
Thumbnail grid with 'tower % of frame' badge and burned-in compass labels
Encroachment table per intersecting cone (view_number, name, overlap m2, ceiling or 'unknown', flips under shift, rationale link)
modules.method: Fetch all 24 City view-cone polygons. Take the shared vertex of cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 as the QE Park viewpoint origin (inference). Read the site placement from site_georeference. Convert lon/lat to EPSG:32610 with proj4js in doubles and subtract a site-centred origin before building three.js cameras. Elevation = terrain at the origin (SITE packet) + eye height. Aim at the tower centroid, zero roll, lens shift to keep verticals vertical; choose focal length so tower share meets the target. Clip the site and tower footprints against every cone (polygon-clipping); build the encroachment report per intersecting cone (overlap, ceiling when known, angular share at that cone's apex); re-run with the footprint shifted one block each way and list flips; send candidates to the M08a breach register. Ray-cast camera to tower top and base against context meshes (three-mesh-bvh) to flag occlusion. Ground presets sit at the site edges named in the brief, eye height 1.6 m. Output camera JSON and compass labels using the rotated north.
modules.human_judgment: Declaring the site placement and checking it against the brief; choosing the mid-city viewpoint, composition, season and time of day; confirming the apex as the designated origin and obtaining cone ceilings; deciding whether to encroach into any cone and writing the rationale; deciding which four ground-level views best show the public realm.
modules.limits: Cone ceiling heights and viewpoint origins were not read: the Public Views Guidelines and 1997 policy returned 403, and the dataset gives polygons only. For triangles the apex is read as the vertex opposite the shortest edge (inference); Clinton Park 28 has five vertices. The site placement comes from the brief or the team. Terrain and context come from the SITE packet. Tree canopy and haze are not modelled.

modules.name: Viewport conditioning capture (depth, line, segmentation)
modules.design_question: Which exact guides (clay beauty, depth, line, tag-colour segmentation) can be rendered from Layer 0 and context so AI renderings stay registered to the massing and its neighbours?
inputs: camera_preset from P13-M03
Layer 0 and context meshes with program tags and existing/approved tower tags
palette mapping program tag and context class to flat colour
sun vector from CLIM packet
target pixel size
outputs: conditioning_pack: {beauty_png, depth_png, line_png, seg_png, palette_json, camera_json, sun_vector, sha256} consumed by P13-M05
pixel-aligned tower mask and context-tower masks used by the fidelity checks

parameters.name: capture_size
parameters.relationship: gpt-image sizes need multiples of 16, ratio between 1:3 and 3:1, edges <= 3840 px and 655,360-8,294,400 pixels; above 2560x1440 is experimental. Larger captures keep thin features but raise token cost.

parameters.name: depth_range_normalisation
parameters.relationship: The diffusers examples min-max normalise depth to 0-1 per image, so the near/far range sets how many grey levels the tower receives; a range spanning the whole city leaves the tower few levels.

parameters.name: line_threshold
parameters.relationship: The diffusers example uses Canny thresholds 100 and 200; lower thresholds keep more edges and tighten structural control, higher ones keep only strong outlines.

parameters.name: segmentation_palette
parameters.relationship: The original ControlNet segmentation model expects ADE20K classes; a custom palette (programme tags plus existing, approved and other context) needs a prompt legend or a fine-tuned model to be interpreted correctly.

parameters.name: controlnet_conditioning_scale
parameters.relationship: In diffusers examples a scale of 0.5 is used; higher values follow the guide image more strictly, lower values give the prompt more freedom and risk geometry drift.

parameters.name: sun_vector
parameters.relationship: The sun in the clay capture sets the shadow direction the render is told to follow; an output with a different sun misstates shading and shadow length relative to the CLIM results.

metrics.name: Size rule compliance (OpenAI route)
metrics.good: all size rules satisfied (multiples of 16; ratio 1:3 to 3:1; edge <= 3840; 655,360-8,294,400 px)
metrics.method: Validate width, height, ratio and pixel count before sending; confirm with one pilot call that the validator matches the API's own error text.
metrics.basis: [evidence: verified | history: r1 flagged as read through a summarising fetch] r2: the raw HTML of the guide (21 Oct 2026) states these constraints for the 2.5 models and for gpt-image-2.

metrics.name: Registration between passes
metrics.good: 0 px offset (same camera, same render call)
metrics.method: Compare silhouette of the depth, line and segmentation passes.
metrics.basis: By construction; checks protect against resize or crop mistakes.

metrics.name: Tagged-pixel completeness
metrics.good: 100% of tower pixels carry a program tag
metrics.method: Count pixels of the 'unknown' colour inside the tower mask.
metrics.basis: Team threshold.

metrics.name: Context-class completeness
metrics.good: every context tower in frame carries an existing or approved tag
metrics.method: Count towers in the ID pass by class against the SITE packet list.
metrics.basis: Team rule so context towers can be checked in the AI output.

metrics.name: Pack completeness
metrics.good: beauty present (OpenAI route); depth + line + segmentation + beauty present (ControlNet route)
metrics.method: Check files and sidecar JSON.
metrics.basis: Route requirements from the ControlNet guide and OpenAI edit endpoint.

visualization: 2x2 contact sheet of beauty, depth (grey ramp with near/far legend), line and segmentation (palette legend by programme and context class)
Opacity slider that overlays any pass on the beauty capture
modules.method: From the chosen camera render passes with identical size and camera in three.js: (1) clay beauty with ambient occlusion and the CLIM sun (core); (2) linear depth normalised between near and far values around tower plus site; (3) line pass from depth/normal discontinuities plus crease edges; (4) ID pass with flat unlit colour per class (programme tags plus existing-context, approved-tower and other-context classes), no anti-aliasing so tags survive. Passes 2-4 are v1. Save PNGs and a JSON sidecar with camera, sun vector, palette, tag counts and SHA-256. Validate size rules before any API call. For fidelity checks later, depth can be re-estimated from the AI output with Depth Anything V2 Small and compared with the exact depth pass.
modules.human_judgment: Which context to include or hide, time of day and sun angle, which landmarks must remain recognisable, and whether the clay capture is a fair representation of the design.
modules.limits: Only programme tags and the context classes above are semantic; trees, water and street furniture have none. ControlNet checkpoints in the cited examples are trained near 512-1024 px, far below board resolution. OpenAI image edits take reference images, not strict control maps, so passes beyond the beauty capture may be only weak hints.

modules.name: Style selection and AI rendering pipeline
modules.design_question: Which style and engine give faithful, site-specific, non-generic renderings from the conditioning pack, at what cost, with what fidelity checks, hosting and honest AI labelling?
inputs: conditioning_pack from P13-M04
camera_preset metadata, context tower list and sun vector
programme and materials from ADVANCED mode
style preset and structured prompt fields
cultural and ecological cues from CULT/ECOL packets
engine choice and API credentials (user-supplied or server-side; never stored in the module)
outputs: render_asset: {image, role skyline|midcity|ground, camera_id, engine, model_snapshot, prompt, seed, size, quality, usage, cost_usd, fidelity{silhouette_iou, edge_match, context_towers_present}, lighting_check, logo_check, ai_label{caption, iptc_digital_source_type (archive copy only)}, accepted}
ai_ledger entry per call consumed by P13-M08a and P13-M06b, including data_retention_setting {default_30d | MAM | ZDR, enabled_for_project, date}

parameters.name: engine
parameters.relationship: OpenAI route: image edit from reference images, no explicit depth or line control. Open route (SDXL/Flux + ControlNet via ComfyUI or diffusers): explicit conditioning scale and local control, but licences and GPU needs differ.

parameters.name: openai_model
parameters.relationship: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst (snapshot 2026-09-08) is described for editing precision, gpt-image-2.5-flare for fast generation, gpt-image-2 (snapshot 2026-04-21) remains; all share token prices. A pinned snapshot id reproduces results.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.relationship: xhigh and max exist only for the 2.5 models; higher quality raises output tokens and cost. Counts of 272, 1,056 and 4,160 output tokens at 1024x1024 (low, medium, high) are published for models before gpt-image-2 only.

parameters.name: size
parameters.relationship: Custom sizes must be multiples of 16 with ratio <= 3:1; above 2560x1440 is experimental. A 3840x2160 output is about 164 px/inch across a 594 mm board, so large heroes may need upscaling.

parameters.name: reference_images
parameters.relationship: gpt-image-2 processes every image input at high fidelity and input_fidelity must be omitted, so each extra reference raises input tokens and cost. The guide's edit example sends four references and states no maximum.

parameters.name: mask_region
parameters.relationship: Masked edits let sky, trees or foreground change while the tower stays; masking is prompt-based and may not follow the mask shape exactly, so protected pixels can still shift.

parameters.name: conditioning_scale (open route)
parameters.relationship: Higher scale keeps output closer to the line/depth guide, lower gives more stylistic freedom; the diffusers examples use 0.5. Architecture-specific tuning evidence was not found.

parameters.name: style_preset
parameters.relationship: Style changes how generic an image looks; the brief says to avoid generic, placeless design, so presets should be anchored by site cues (City in Nature, mountains, water) chosen by the team. Effect on jury score is not evidenced.

parameters.name: moderation
parameters.relationship: 'auto' applies standard filtering; blocked requests return moderation_blocked and must not be retried without changing the inputs.

parameters.name: deployment
parameters.relationship: A static page cannot hold an OpenAI key safely: a thin server proxy keeps it server-side; a user key in memory still sits in page scripts. SAM 2 and ComfyUI need a Python/GPU service, local or rented per second.

parameters.name: data_retention
parameters.relationship: Abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default. Zero data retention is an organisation or project setting needing prior OpenAI approval; the 2.5 models, gpt-image-2 and older are listed as compatible. Inputs flagged by the CSAM scan are kept regardless.

metrics.name: Tower silhouette IoU (fidelity)
metrics.method: Segment the AI output with SAM 2 prompted by the projected tower box, then compare with the tower mask from the conditioning segmentation pass (or use the depth-difference method alone).
metrics.basis: No published benchmark for architectural fidelity; team thresholds, tune on pilot renders.

metrics.name: Line agreement
metrics.good: >= 0.80 of conditioning line pixels within 3 px of an output edge
metrics.method: Edge-detect the output and compute the proportion of guide-line pixels with an output edge within a tolerance.
metrics.basis: Team thresholds.

metrics.name: Storey / bay count match (hero views)
metrics.good: visible storey lines equal the model
metrics.method: Human tick in the review step, assisted by overlaying the model's floor lines.
metrics.basis: A rendering must not misrepresent the design; team rule.

metrics.name: Context towers present in output
metrics.good: all existing and approved towers in frame are present (box IoU >= 0.5 with the ID-pass mask) and none invented
metrics.method: SAM 2 masks prompted by each context-tower box, compared with the conditioning ID pass; list differences for the reviewer.
metrics.basis: The brief (as transcribed) puts existing and approved towers of 244-305 m in the context; the 0.5 cut-off is a team value.

metrics.name: No invented marks in output
metrics.good: human check finds no logos, crests, signage text or watermarks in an accepted render
metrics.bad: any invented mark, or check not logged
metrics.method: Reviewer inspects the render at 100% zoom; result stored in render_asset.logo_check.
metrics.basis: Terms 5.1 bars marks, logos, symbols or signs that may identify the source; AI renders can invent signage.

metrics.name: Lighting consistency
metrics.good: shadows and highlights agree with the CLIM sun vector (human tick against an overlaid arrow)
metrics.method: Reviewer compares the output with the sun-vector overlay; no automated estimator is specified.
metrics.basis: Renders can invent a sun direction; no sourced estimator was found (see unresolved_relationships).

metrics.name: Cost per accepted image
metrics.good: <= team budget set from pilot calls (>= 5 per quality level)
metrics.method: (text_in x 5 + image_in x 8 + image_out x 30) / 10^6 per image at standard rates (batch is half); token counts read from the response usage object.
metrics.basis: Token rates verified; per-image token counts for the 2.5 models are unpublished and edits with references raise input tokens, so the budget must come from logged pilots.

metrics.name: AI label and ledger coverage
metrics.good: 100% of AI-derived images carry a visible caption and a ledger entry
metrics.method: Join render_asset records with board placements.
metrics.basis: Good practice from journal disclosure rules and EU Article 50 principles; Buildner's terms read contain no AI rule.

metrics.name: Retention setting logged
metrics.good: every ledger row records the provider, the retention setting actually in force (default 30-day, Modified Abuse Monitoring or ZDR, with whether it is enabled for the project) and the date
metrics.bad: any row without it, or a row that assumes ZDR without an approved project setting
metrics.method: Check ledger fields against the project's actual OpenAI data-controls setting.
metrics.basis: [rule: team control; facts verified r3 | history: r2 said the 2.5 models were not ZDR-listed (F36)] Unpublished competition designs go to a third party; the data-controls page lists gpt-image-2.5-sunburst and -flare as ZDR compatible, but ZDR and MAM need prior OpenAI approval and are not the default; 30-day abuse-monitoring retention applies otherwise and CSAM-scanned inputs are retained even under ZDR.

metrics.name: Provenance signal present in API output
metrics.good: C2PA and/or SynthID detected on the returned image
metrics.method: Read manifest with a C2PA reader; check OpenAI's verification page manually.
metrics.basis: Help-centre text (not opened; search excerpt) says API images carry C2PA metadata and SynthID, with coverage varying and metadata strippable; the image guide has no C2PA statement.

visualization: Side-by-side slider of conditioning beauty and AI output with a difference overlay (line mismatches in red, silhouette misses in amber) and a sun-vector arrow
Metric badges (IoU, line agreement, context towers, cost) each linked to the threshold source or an amber 'team assumption' tag
Gallery with 'AI' badge, model snapshot, prompt, cost and retention setting (default, MAM or ZDR) on each card; running cost meter
modules.method: 1) User picks camera preset, style preset, engine and deployment. 2) A structured prompt is built from fields (materials, season, time of day, weather, entourage) with a block-list: no logos, signage, team names, real-person likenesses or imitation of Indigenous art. 3) OpenAI route (core): the proxy calls POST /v1/images/edits with a pinned snapshot, prompt, image[] = clay capture, size, quality; input_fidelity omitted on gpt-image-2. Open route (v1): ComfyUI /prompt (ControlNet depth + line) or diffusers; keep the seed. 4) Fidelity: SAM 2 masks, IoU, line agreement, context towers; sun-vector overlay for a human check; human check for invented marks. 5) Ledger row: snapshot, parameters, prompt, hashes, usage, cost, retention setting actually in force. 6) Caption. 7) Human accepts or rejects; rejected renders stay in the ledger.

parameters.name: export_dpi
parameters.relationship: Pixels = mm / 25.4 x dpi: 150 dpi = 3508 x 2480 (9.2 bits/px available at 10^7 bytes), 200 dpi = 4677 x 3307 (5.2), 300 dpi = 7016 x 4961 (2.3; computed). Higher dpi keeps hairlines crisp but forces lower JPEG quality.

parameters.name: jpeg_quality_search
parameters.relationship: The encoder searches the highest quality that stays under the byte target; lower quality shrinks bytes but adds ringing around thin linework and small type. The curve depends on content, so it is measured, not predicted.

parameters.name: chroma_subsampling
parameters.relationship: 4:2:0 halves chroma resolution and smears thin coloured linework and small coloured type; 4:4:4 keeps them but costs bytes. sharp defaults to 4:2:0; jSquash MozJPEG defaults to progressive with chroma_subsample 2, so set both explicitly.

parameters.name: jpeg_scan_mode
parameters.relationship: Portal handling of progressive JPEG is undocumented, so baseline is the default. Bytes differ by mode and content; measure both on the real board before choosing.

parameters.name: type_scale
parameters.relationship: At fit-to-width on a 1920 px screen, 594 mm = 3.23 px/mm, so 2.5 mm lettering is about 8 px and 3.5 mm about 11 px; smaller text becomes unreadable if the jury views boards on screen (assumed).

parameters.name: placed_image_scale
parameters.relationship: Effective resolution = image width in px / placed width in inches; enlarging an AI render past its native pixels lowers effective dpi and softens detail.

parameters.name: metadata_policy
parameters.unit: strip all | keep IPTC source type
parameters.relationship: Creator names, software strings and manifests can reveal authors, and Terms 5.1 bars identifying marks. sharp removes metadata by default and ExifTool -all= is not guaranteed complete, so every export is re-scanned.

parameters.name: ai_label_placement
parameters.relationship: A visible caption beside each AI-derived image is the operative label; metadata is stripped on export and can be removed anyway. EU AI Act Art. 50 asks for clear disclosure but is marked amended and is only a benchmark.

parameters.name: font_glyph_coverage
parameters.relationship: Nation names need combining marks and modifier letters; a font without them substitutes glyphs and misspells the name. Charis SIL is OFL-licensed and aimed at linguistic text, but coverage must be tested per code point.

parameters.name: deny_list_terms
parameters.relationship: Each per-team seed (names, school, firm, course codes, email domains) catches one more identifier (Terms 5.1) but adds OCR false positives that block export; findings are cleared with a logged reason. Juror names and practices form a warn-only class W.

parameters.name: visual_check
parameters.relationship: A text scan misses crests, logos, watermarks and invented signage, which Terms 5.1 also bars. A per-board human check at 100% zoom catches them; optional template matching only finds team-supplied logos.

metrics.name: Bytes per board (hard limit)
metrics.good: <= 10^7 bytes
metrics.method: Measure final file; loop quality and pixel size until under the target.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-02 | same record as P13-M01] Terms 4.8 limit of 10 MB; MB not defined, so the stricter 10^7 bytes is used.

metrics.name: Bytes per board (team target)
metrics.good: <= 9.5 x 10^6 bytes
metrics.method: Same measurement against the margin.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-02t] Team margin for MB/MiB and portal overhead; editable.

metrics.name: File format
metrics.good: JPEG
metrics.method: Magic bytes and extension.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-01] Terms 4.8.

metrics.name: Pixel ratio
metrics.method: width_px / height_px.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-04 | same record as P13-M01: A2 verified; landscape unverified until register; tolerance team-set | history: r1 corrected] One record, so M01 and M06 cannot disagree.

metrics.name: JPEG encoding settings
metrics.good: baseline, 4:4:4, sRGB, no metadata
metrics.bad: progressive or 4:2:0 used without a test
metrics.method: Read SOF marker (FFC0 baseline, FFC2 progressive) and component sampling factors from the file.
metrics.basis: Portal acceptance is undocumented; a live test upload is unsafe, so ask the organiser before 3 Nov (C2).

metrics.name: Validator parser agreement
metrics.good: own SOF parser agrees with sharp metadata() (chromaSubsampling, isProgressive) on fixtures for baseline/progressive x 4:2:0/4:4:4
metrics.method: Unit test on four fixture JPEGs.
metrics.basis: Wikipedia lists SOF0 = FFC0 and SOF2 = FFC2; the byte-level sampling encoding was not read, so the test settles it.

metrics.name: Effective resolution of each placed raster
metrics.good: >= 150 px/inch at 594 mm board width
metrics.method: native px / placed inches for every image.
metrics.basis: Team print/screen target; no jury requirement found.

metrics.name: Smallest text height
metrics.good: >= 3.5 mm on the board (about 11 px at 1920 px width)
metrics.method: Scan text frames and SVG text; report min cap height.
metrics.basis: 2.5 mm and 3.5 mm are nominal lettering sizes in the technical-lettering series; they are not a legibility rule for boards.

metrics.name: Anonymity findings
metrics.good: 0 class-A findings in file name, EXIF/XMP/ICC and OCR text matching the per-team deny-list; every class-W juror-name warning cleared with a logged reason
metrics.bad: >= 1 class-A finding; an uncleared class-W warning is amber
metrics.method: Re-read the exported JPEG metadata and OCR tiles of the raster for deny-list strings; seeds are generated per team from its registration data (for the course team: member names, UBC, SALA, ARCH 540, instructors, email domains); class W seeds are juror names and practices.
metrics.basis: [rule HR-06] Terms 5.1: no marks that may identify authority or source; 5.2 and 8.3 bar approaching or communicating with jurors. Whether citing a juror's own building counts as an approach is unresolved (C8), so class W warns and does not block. The scan method and seeds are the team's design.

metrics.name: Visual anonymity check
metrics.good: each board has a logged check at 100% zoom for logos, crests, watermarks and signage by a member who did not compose it
metrics.method: Checkbox per board in the release strip; optional OpenCV template matching of team-supplied logos.
metrics.basis: Terms 5.1 names marks, logos, symbols and signs; OCR cannot see them.

metrics.name: Glyph coverage
metrics.good: 100% of code points in text frames and the allow-list exist in the loaded fonts (NFC-normalised)
metrics.method: Compare each text run's code points with the font cmap before rasterising; on the validator route, the check is a human look at Nation names at 100% zoom.
metrics.basis: Team rule to protect Nation names; OCR cannot be relied on for these orthographies.

metrics.name: AI-derived images with visible label
metrics.method: Compare render_asset list with placements and caption frames.
metrics.basis: Disclosure practice; Buildner terms read contain no AI rule.

visualization: Validator drop zone: one card per JPEG with pass/amber/fail chips per rule id, byte gauge (bytes against 10^7 and 9.5 x 10^6), pixel ratio, SOF scan and sampling, metadata fields found, OCR findings pinned on a thumbnail (class A red, class W juror warnings amber)
WYSIWYG board canvas with snap grid and four-board overview strip (M06a thin form in core, composer v1)
Overlays: text-size heat map (red below 2.5 mm), per-image effective-dpi flags, glyph-fallback markers, anonymity findings pinned to the image
Side-by-side 'what the jury sees' preview at 1920 px width and at 100% zoom
Release strip per board showing gate state (open, passed, visual check done, signed N of N)
modules.method: M06v (core, 6 Nov): drop one or more JPEGs; read magic bytes, byte length, pixel size, SOF marker, sampling factors, ICC and EXIF/XMP/IPTC fields (browser: own parser plus exifr; Node: sharp metadata and ExifTool); OCR tiles with tesseract.js against the per-team deny-list, the juror register (warn only) and an English check; write export_manifest. M06a (core, thin): JSON scene in mm, element tags, text frames with language attestation, panel-rule check. M06b (v1): compose each scene into one 594 x 420 mm SVG, rasterise with resvg, convert to sRGB, encode MozJPEG baseline 4:4:4 without metadata, lowering quality from 95 toward 70 and then pixel size until under the target; proof PDF with pdf-lib. M06c: release the package only when P13-M01 reports blocking=false, N members signed and every board has a logged visual check; the tool never uploads.
modules.human_judgment: Composition, narrative order, visual hierarchy and what to show; final QA at 100% zoom including the visual anonymity check; whether captions and disclosures are placed well; font licences; clearing or acting on juror-name warnings; the upload to the Buildner portal.
modules.limits: Buildner pixel, colour-mode, progressive and MB/MiB rules are not documented in the pages read; a live test upload is unsafe because the first upload locks edits. Browser canvas size limits were not verified, so use WASM or a server path for composing. JPEG is lossy near the size cap; PDF is a proof only. OCR of Nation-name orthographies is unreliable and logo detection finds only supplied templates.

modules.name: Jury-criteria self-assessment rubric
modules.design_question: How well do the design and board set address each weighted jury criterion, and what cited evidence supports every self-score?
inputs: jury criteria and sub-criteria with weights 40/30/20/10 (brief as transcribed; unverified until the register)
evidence links to module results from all packets, each with metric, threshold and source
board_layout tags and area share per criterion from P13-M06a (optional in core: area shares typed by hand)
human scores on a 0-4 scale
breach register (departures from policy and guidelines) with rationale from P13-M08a
award tracks: Sustainability Award and Student Award (eligibility text from the brief, not obtained)
outputs: rubric_state: {scores[], evidence[], gaps[], weighted_total, attention_ratio[], award_evidence[]} consumed by P13-M08b and, as optional advisory gaps, P13-M01
evidence table for the policy reflection

parameters.name: criterion_weights
parameters.relationship: One point on the 0-4 scale is worth 10 points of 100 for human-scale (40%) but 2.5 points for urban integration (10%), so effort and board space should follow the weights. Weights are unverified until the register.

parameters.name: level_descriptors
parameters.relationship: UNRESOLVED: effect of descriptor wording on rater agreement was not found in an opened source (see unresolved_relationships).

parameters.name: evidence_tier
parameters.unit: A measured | B visual | C narrative
parameters.relationship: Higher-tier evidence supports a higher score; a score of 3 or more without tier-A or tier-B evidence is flagged as unsupported (team rule).

parameters.name: board_area_share
parameters.relationship: The share of board area used for a criterion should track its weight; a 30%-weight criterion with 5% area is under-communicated, which matters because the jury sees only the boards.

parameters.name: breach_register
parameters.relationship: The brief says the jury may reward justified breaches of guidelines, so each departure needs a stated reason and evidence; unexplained departures count against the criterion they touch.

parameters.name: award_tracks
parameters.relationship: Sustainability and Student Awards (CAD 1,000 each) are separate prizes; an entry in the top three that wins either takes both prizes. Tracking their evidence (CLIM/ENER results) costs effort but can win a prize.

metrics.name: Weighted self-score
metrics.good: no cut-off: shown as a plain number labelled 'team heuristic'
metrics.method: sum over criteria of weight x score/4 x 100.
metrics.basis: Weights from the brief as transcribed (unverified until the register); earlier 75/50 cut-offs had no anchor and are removed; the result is not a prediction of jury outcome.

metrics.name: Evidence coverage per criterion
metrics.good: >= 3 items incl. >= 1 measured and >= 1 visual
metrics.method: Count linked evidence by tier.
metrics.basis: Team rule supporting the course requirement to cite sources and show work.

metrics.name: Board attention ratio
metrics.method: (area share of criterion) / (weight share).
metrics.basis: Team heuristic.

metrics.name: Rater disagreement
metrics.good: |score A - score B| <= 1 on the 0-4 scale
metrics.method: Two team members score independently; compare.
metrics.basis: Team threshold; no reliability literature is relied on.

metrics.name: Site-specific evidence count (anti-generic)
metrics.good: >= 3 items tied to the site (landscape, climate, history, Indigenous perspectives) per cultural-context sub-criterion
metrics.method: Count evidence tagged 'site-specific' by the author.
metrics.basis: The brief asks to avoid generic, placeless design; threshold is team-set.

metrics.name: Award evidence (Sustainability Award)
metrics.good: >= 3 linked items incl. >= 1 measured CLIM/ENER result
metrics.method: Count evidence tagged 'sustainability'.
metrics.basis: Award exists (competition page); its judging text is in the brief and was not obtained; threshold is team-set.

visualization: Four-axis radar chart plus a bar whose width follows weight (40/30/20/10); the total is printed as a plain number with a 'team heuristic' label, with no good/bad colouring
Stacked evidence bars per criterion by tier; evidence table with metric, threshold, source link
Board heat strip showing which criterion each element supports; version history of scores
modules.method: Store criteria, sub-criteria, descriptors and evidence links as data. Each evidence item points to a module id, metric name, value, threshold and source id, or to a board element tagged in P13-M06a (core: area shares typed by hand if M06a is absent). Humans enter 0-4 scores with a one-line justification. The tool computes the weighted total, tier counts and board attention ratio and flags: score >= 3 without tier-A/B evidence, criterion with zero evidence, high weight with low area share, large gap between two raters, breaches without rationale (from the P13-M08a register). Optional award tracks list their evidence separately. Scores are never computed or filled by an AI; an optional assistant may only suggest existing results as evidence, and the suggestion is logged. Every threshold shows its source or an amber 'team assumption' tag.
modules.human_judgment: All scores and their interpretation, especially human-scale experience, cultural context and reconciliation, which need lived knowledge and Indigenous perspectives; deciding which breaches to make and justify; interpreting what the jury will value.
modules.limits: No published VTC scoring scale or past jury scores were found; weights are from the brief PDF as transcribed. The jury-panel page lists seven jurors and says nothing on scoring. Terms 10.4 describe a shortlist stage before Guest Jury ranking. Self-scores are biased and unvalidated; the rubric measures evidence coverage, not design quality. M07 is v1: core modules must not require it.

modules.design_question: How can the tool help the team write the policy reflection from cited evidence while words stay human, every AI use is disclosed, every board image's licence is known and nothing is published early?
inputs: module results and source lists from all packets
ai_ledger entries from P13-M05 (M08a)
asset metadata: source, author, licence, licence URL, evidence file, visibility for every raster (M08a)
review_audience_log typed by the team: {date, venue, viewers by role, assets shown} for every course review, crit or desk review (M08a)
juror_register from the document_register (names and practices from the jury-panel snapshot) (M08a)
breach entries typed by humans and encroachment_report candidates from P13-M03 (M08a)
rubric_state from P13-M07 (M08b only, optional)
team notes and drafts typed by humans
Higher Buildings Policy documents and Public Views Guidelines (reference list)
