parameters.name: assistance_level
parameters.relationship: L0 evidence pack only, L1 outline and questions, L2 critique of a human draft, L3 AI-drafted text (off by default). Higher levels reduce the human share of authorship and raise the disclosure and originality risk.

parameters.name: claim_traceability
parameters.relationship: Each number or policy claim must link to a module result and its source; untraceable numbers are shown as team assumptions or flagged FALSE ASSUMPTION if later disproved, so unsupported claims cannot enter boards silently.

parameters.name: governing_policy_set
parameters.relationship: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is under review (Phase 1 early directions; Phase 2 draft policies fall 2026 to early 2027; no update adopted); protected views are not under review. The reflection must name the document it assesses against.

parameters.name: text_length
parameters.relationship: More words per board lower the type size that fits; the board layout caps legible text, so length trades against the 2.5-3.5 mm text-height targets in P13-M06.

parameters.name: disclosure_detail
parameters.relationship: Journal-style rules require disclosing AI tool use and keep humans responsible for output; a detailed ledger makes the statement accurate and supports the course rule to show work.

parameters.name: identity_exposure
parameters.relationship: A C2PA signing certificate identifies the signer, so signing exported boards with a personal identity would conflict with anonymity; labels use generic visible captions, with IPTC source-type fields kept only in archive copies.

parameters.name: licence_status
parameters.relationship: Terms 4.3 lets Buildner demand image licences, and failure to supply them may disqualify; 12.2 and 12.7 grant Buildner perpetual promotional and publication licences, so each raster needs a licence that allows them. Unknown means blocking.

parameters.name: ai_tool_terms
parameters.relationship: AI outputs carry tool terms and model licences: FLUX [dev] weights are non-commercial, SDXL's Open RAIL++-M allows commercial use with passed-on restrictions, OpenAI terms were not read. Buildner advises against treating AI images as sole work.

parameters.name: explanation_request
parameters.relationship: If Buildner asks for the design process, sources of inspiration and evolution of ideas (Terms 4.1.5), a dated ledger and breach register can answer directly instead of being reconstructed.

parameters.name: asset_visibility
parameters.relationship: Terms 4.1 bars visuals already published by a member; 5.2, 5.3 and 8.3 bar approaching jurors and hide identities until winners. Default entry-private; every review logs its audience, and a listed juror among viewers sets G-04 red.

metrics.name: Rights register completeness
metrics.good: 100% of placed rasters have source, author, licence, licence URL or evidence hash, and a yes on 'licensable to Buildner under Terms 12.2 and 12.7'
metrics.bad: any raster with unknown licence (blocks release)
metrics.method: Join placements from P13-M06a with register rows; licence pack export lists evidence for each.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.3 (licences on request, failure may disqualify) and 12.2/12.7; the register columns are team design.

metrics.name: Entry-private default and juror exposure
metrics.good: 0 board-linked assets with visibility public before 2026-11-30T23:59Z, and every review in the audience log lists no listed juror among the viewers
metrics.bad: >= 1 public board-linked asset, or a listed juror among the viewers of one
metrics.method: Check asset_visibility on every asset linked to a board element and the review_audience_log against the juror_register; sharing needs a logged override.
metrics.basis: Tool design to avoid the previous-publication risk (Terms 4.1) and juror contact or exposure (5.2, 5.3, 8.3); Buildner's own reading of 'published' and of a juror attending a course review is unresolved.

metrics.name: Encroachment entries with rationale
metrics.good: 100% of view-cone encroachments from P13-M03 (any of the 24 cones) have a breach entry with a written reason
metrics.method: Join encroachment_report with breach_register.
metrics.basis: The brief (as transcribed) says justified breaches may be rewarded; unexplained ones are weak evidence.

metrics.name: Traceable-claim ratio
metrics.good: 100% of numeric claims linked to a source or flagged team assumption
metrics.method: Regex-detect numbers and policy names; check for a claim link.
metrics.basis: Course requirement to cite sources; cut-offs are team values.

metrics.name: Human-authored share of final text
metrics.good: 100% of final prose typed or edited by a team member (levels L0-L2 only)
metrics.bad: any AI-originated sentence not reviewed and disclosed
metrics.method: Compare diff log provenance tags per paragraph.
metrics.basis: Informed by journal guidance that AI is not an author and humans are accountable; not a Buildner rule.

metrics.name: AI-use ledger completeness
metrics.good: 100% of AI calls (text and image) logged with model, date, purpose, input/output hash and retention setting actually in force
metrics.method: Compare API call log with ledger rows.
metrics.basis: Disclosure principle from ICMJE guidance.

metrics.name: Breach rationale coverage
metrics.good: 100% of flagged breaches have a written justification
metrics.method: Join breach register with text_blocks (v1) or the typed text frames in P13-M06a (core).
metrics.basis: Brief says justified breaches may be rewarded (as transcribed).

metrics.name: Identifying strings in text
metrics.good: 0 matches against the per-team deny-list; juror-register matches shown as warnings and cleared with a reason
metrics.method: String match; the OCR pass in P13-M06v repeats it on the raster.
metrics.basis: Terms 5.1 bars identifying marks; 5.2 and 8.3 bar approaching jurors.

metrics.name: IPTC source type on archive copies of AI images
metrics.good: trainedAlgorithmicMedia for generated images; compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia for edits such as inpainting
metrics.bad: absent or wrong in the archive copy
metrics.method: Write and read XMP-iptcExt DigitalSourceType with ExifTool on the component images kept in the course archive; board JPEGs are scrubbed.
metrics.basis: IPTC vocabulary definitions; the tag exists in ExifTool's XMP-iptcExt table; the visible caption is the operative label on boards; a human decides which value applies.

visualization: Three-pane editor: evidence pack with source chips; human draft with provenance underline (none = human, amber = AI-suggested); ledger timeline
Claim linter badges beside each sentence (linked, team assumption, unsupported)
Rights table with a traffic light per board image (known, unknown, restricted) and a visibility column (entry-private, public, reviewed-by-juror flag), plus a licence-pack download
Policy checklist with pass / exceed / breach per policy item and a justification field; encroachment rows imported from P13-M03
modules.method: M08a (core, upstream of P13-M07): 1) every AI call from P13-M05 writes a JSONL ledger row (model snapshot, date, purpose, input/output hashes, retention setting actually in force, reviewer); 2) rights register: each raster gets source, author, licence, licence URL, evidence hash, visibility (default entry-private) and a Terms 12.2 answer; unknown licences or public or juror-seen board-linked assets set blocking in P13-M01; 3) review_audience_log: every course review or crit records its viewers, matched against the juror register; 4) breach entries need a rationale; encroachment candidates from P13-M03 appear here; 5) captions for AI images, IPTC source type only in archive copies. M08b (v1, downstream of P13-M07): 6) evidence pack with source chips; 7) team-authored question templates; 8) provenance per paragraph, AI limited to L0-L2; 9) linter flags numbers or policy names without a claim link; 10) language attested English, Nation names via the allow-list with gloss; 11) text blocks go to P13-M06b through an optional port; in core the team types text frames in P13-M06a.
modules.human_judgment: All prose, positions and ethical stance; whether any AI text is used; reconciliation and Indigenous perspectives, which should draw on community knowledge, not generated text; the final policy reflection; whether to encroach and the rationale; who attends a review while the entry is live; the legal check on rights and tool terms; confirming the course's own AI rules.
modules.limits: No sourced benchmark defines a good policy reflection. Buildner's terms contain no AI rule and its FAQ advises caution, so the team's disclosure standard is a choice. UBC course guidance returned 404. EU AI Act Article 50 is a benchmark only (marked amended, Digital Omnibus changes not read; binding force for a Canadian entry assumed absent). Whether the organiser counts community-area posts as publication is unknown.

flags.claim: Hidden lines can be obtained as 'all projected edges minus visible' with a clipper2-js difference.
flags.correction: Clip projected edges against the polygons of nearer occluding faces, or subtract collinear visible sub-segments from each edge by parameter intervals with a tolerance; keep the hidden class Make2D-only until a pilot comparison passes.
flags.detail: Clipper2: only subject paths may be open and clip paths must be closed, so a set of open segments cannot be subtracted from another set of open segments. P13-S25 uses clipper2-js for silhouette polygons, not for line differencing.

flags.detail: MDN: longOffset returns the long localized GMT format such as 'GMT-08:00', so a literal '-07:00' comparison never matches and always shows the fallback warning. The latest tzdb release is 2026e and the 2026b basis for BC still holds.
